name: The Seer's Riddle
descriptionTemplate: {Team Unique}: The wielder's Fixed {Corrosion} effects +[StateArg1]%, and Fixed HP Recovery from Exalt +[StateArg2]%. After the wielder releases Exalt, gain Temporary {STR} equal to [StateArg3]% of their current Permanent {STR}. 3-turn cooldown.
lore:
Vivian did not belong among these people, and she had known it from an early age. Their minds turned too slowly, and they worried about far too many things. She could probably have managed the whole tangled business of who was related to whom and who wasn't speaking to whom this week, but those were the least, LEAST important things in the world.

Every so often, a strange idea would bubble up in her head. The world was one enormous cauldron, and everything else was ingredients for a potion. Distill it, and you got honor. Freeze it, and you got history. Give it a good stir, and you got love. And at the very end, after a very long time, what you had brewed was an eternity of bitterness.

Why else would everything enjoyable be bad for you, and every reward worth having demand more hardship than anyone could imagine?

The only sweet, dependable thing in the world was sleep, the easiest minimum wage any living creature could earn.

So when she was chosen by Aequidan's ancient sacred temple, she wasn't the least bit surprised.

She disliked dealing with people so much that, naturally, she'd be expected to use the Seer's power to cook up misery.

Elixir or Poison. Pick a side. Then, once in your life, you may pick the other.

"It's a once-in-a-lifetime offer, you know."

The Seer gave a gurgling chuckle from the shadows.

She chose the Elixir.

The Seer, now obliged to share Their power with her, leapt into her arms, croaking with fury.

"You tricked me! You two-faced little fraud! With the gloomy streak you keep tucked away, you should've picked poison without a second thought! You were supposed to spend your whole life wandering further and further down forbidden paths, become a witch whose name sent people running, then stumble across the one person who could redeem your soul, be deeply moved, and finally use your once-in-a-lifetime chance to brew an elixir and save them."

"And then I'd tell you the chance was fake, and you'd both die in despair. That's how it was supposed to go!"

"So whichever side I picked, I'd only ever have been able to brew poison?"

"Of course not. This is a genuine contract. Even I can't break it."

"Then... that means I don't actually get one chance to brew poison either?"

The Seer said nothing. Well, the chance was still there. When someone who had spent her whole life brewing elixirs finally decided to distill a single drop of bitterness...

Ah, it would be a magnificent poison, for sure.
